# Instruction Safety

**Claim.** Every active deterministic instruction generated by the program satisfies the stated register-distinctness, valid-input, and pairwise-distinct-call-argument conditions; inactive configurations and choice instructions impose no additional condition.

**Proof.** If the configuration has no active control label, the safety predicate is true by definition. For an active label, inspect the program instruction at that label. At the round labels, the only relevant cases reduce to clearing a register or to the explicit register comparison; the two registers in that comparison are distinct. At every other label, unfolding the instruction and the safety predicate verifies the required condition directly: comparisons use distinct registers, calls list distinct argument registers, and there are no input-payload comparisons requiring a validity hypothesis. Labels carrying nondeterministic choices are replaced by a fixed return instruction when forming the deterministic part, so they likewise create no safety obligation. Thus all possible labels satisfy the predicate.
